title: A magnitude 7.1 earthquake with an epicentre in neighbouring Tibet shakes parts of Nepal, injuring at least 13 people across the country.
text: On 7 January 2025 at 09:05 CST, an earthquake measuring Mw 7.1 struck Tingri County, located in the Shigatse prefecture-level city of the Tibet Autonomous Region of Southwestern China. Between 126 and 400 people were killed and 338 were injured in the region.

title: The Supreme Court of Nepal strikes down several laws that allowed for the construction of hydropower and hotel projects in protected nature reserves.
text: The Supreme Court of Nepal is the highest court in Nepal. It is designated as the court of record by the Constitution of Nepal.

title: An Austrian climber is reported dead on Ama Dablam after going missing on 26 April.
text: Ama Dablam is a mountain in the Eastern Himalayas range of Koshi Province, Nepal. The main peak is 6,812 metres (22,349 ft), the lower western peak is 6,170 metres (20,243 ft).

title: An American climber dies after suffering a cardiac arrest while descending from Makalu.
text: Cardiac arrest, also known as sudden cardiac arrest, is a condition in which the heart suddenly and unexpectedly stops beating or beats in a way which fails to produce pulse. When the heart stops, blood cannot circulate properly through the body and the blood flow to the brain and other organs is decreased.

title: The European Union adds Nepal to its list of high risk jurisdictions for money laundering and terrorism financing.
text: The European Union is a political and economic union of 27 member states that are located primarily in Europe. A supranational union with a total area of 4,233,255 km2 (1,634,469 sq mi) and an estimated population of just under 452 million as of 2026, its member states generated a nominal gross domestic product (GDP) of around €18.802 trillion in 2025, accounting for approximately one sixth of global economic output.

title: The Friendship Bridge connecting Nepal's Rasuwa District with China is swept away due to flooding along the Bhotekoshi River, killing nine people and leaving 19 others missing.
text: Bhote Koshi in Nepal and Poiqu in Tibet is the name given to the upper course (main tributary) of the Sun Koshi river. It is part of the Koshi River system in Nepal.

title: Heavy monsoon rains trigger sudden floods and landslidess nationwide, killing at least 41 people and injuring 121 others, according to the national disaster management authority.
text: A monsoon is traditionally a seasonal reversing wind accompanied by corresponding changes in precipitation, but now used to describe seasonal changes in atmospheric circulation and precipitation associated with annual latitudinal oscillation of the Intertropical Convergence Zone, specifically between its limits to the north and south of the equator. Usually, the term monsoon is used to refer to the rainy phase of …

title: The government orders the blocking of 24 social media platforms including Facebook, X and YouTube for failing to register with it.
text: YouTube is an American online video-sharing platform owned by Google. YouTube was founded on February 14, 2005, by Chad Hurley, Jawed Karim, and Steve Chen, all of whom were former employees at PayPal.

title: Nationwide protests are carried out by youths primarily against the social media ban and corruption. Clashes with police initially kill at least 72 people and injure over 2,100. The unrest prompts the resignation of Home Minister Ramesh…
text: In September 2025, large-scale anti-corruption protests and demonstrations took place all across Nepal, predominantly organized by Generation Z students and young citizens. Known as the "Gen Z Revolution" or "Third People's Movement", they began parallel to a nationwide ban on numerous social media platforms including YouTube, Instagram, TikTok, X, Facebook, and WhatsApp, and were motivated by the public's frustra…

title: K. P. Sharma Oli resigns as prime minister following the 2025 Nepalese Gen Z protests.
text: Khadga Prasad Sharma Oli better known as K.P. Sharma Oli, is a Nepali politician who served three terms as the prime minister of Nepal, from 2015 to 2016, 2018 to 2021, and 2024 to 2025. He has served as the chairman of the Communist Party of Nepal (Unified Marxist–Leninist) since 2014.

title: The headquarters of the Federal Parliament of Nepal, multiple government buildings and the residences of leading politicians in Kathmandu are set on fire by antigovernment protesters.
text: The Federal Parliament of Nepal is the bicameral federal and supreme legislature of Nepal established in 2018 (2074 BS). It consists of the National Assembly and the House of Representatives as parallel houses.

title: Former chief justice Sushila Karki is appointed as interim prime minister, making her the first woman to hold the office.
text: Sushila Karki is a Nepalese lawyer and stateswoman who served as chief justice of Nepal from 2016 to 2017 and as interim prime minister of Nepal from 2025 to 2026. She became prime minister following the youth protests of September 2025 that led to her predecessor's resignation.

title: Polish climber Andrzej Bargiel becomes the first person to ski down Mount Everest without the use of supplemental oxygen.
text: Andrzej Leszek Bargiel is a Polish ski mountaineer, backcountry skier, mountain runner and climber, who became the first person in history to climb and ski from the summit of Everest without any bottled oxygen. Raised in Łętownia, he is a three-time Polish ski mountaineering champion and held third place in the overall World Cup.

title: Two-year-old Aryatara Shakya is installed as the new Kumari Devi in Kathmandu, succeeding Trishna Shakya who held the position since 2017.
text: Devi Kanya Kumari (Sanskrit: देवी कन्या कुमारि, romanized: Dēvi Kanyā Kumāri) is a manifestation of the Hindu goddess Mahadevi in the form of an adolescent girl. She is variously described by various traditions of Hinduism to be a form of Parvati.

title: A South Korean climber is killed in a storm on Mera Peak.
text: Mera Peak is a mountain in the Mahalangur section, Barun sub-section of the Himalaya and administratively in Nepal's Sagarmatha Zone, Sankhuwasabha. At 6,476 metres it is classified as a trekking peak.

title: The remains of Bipin Joshi, a student who died in captivity in the Gaza Strip after being abducted by Hamas in the 7 October attacks, are repatriated to Nepal.
text: On October 7, 2023, a series of coordinated armed incursions from the blockaded Gaza Strip into the Gaza envelope of southern Israel were carried out by Hamas and several other Palestinian militant groups. In response, Israel launched a major military operation in Gaza.
